result:
I made the figure modules, the five sheets and the three looping MP4s in `/workspace/tesla-factory/v3/figures/`, plus the short plan update. I looked at every sheet and animation strip and fixed the obvious problems.

**Checks I ran**
- **Feet don't slide during walks:** I measured this numerically and the planted foot moves 0 m. That's by design: footsteps are fixed to the ground and the body moves over them.
- **Hands and feet reach their targets:** checked at 201 points in each of the 12 figure motions; none fell short.
- **Loops are seamless:** for all three MP4s, the first frame and the frame at the end are pixel-identical.
- **Natural movement:** elbows bend backwards and down, knees forward, arms swing opposite the legs, heels strike and toes push off.

**Part A — plan update**
- **42:** there is now only one, a small red plate on the ship skirt just below the cargo door. Its fall and the turkey/Shiba table gag are merged into one gag (period 127 s). The 42 lands on the tank-farm grating next to the lawn, so the clang spooks the flock. Elon still makes the replacement and hangs it back. The spare 42 and the inspector are cut.
- **Robot feast:** new gag (period 89 s) at the back of room 3C. An Optimus cooks bolts, grease and AA batteries, then eats them.
- **Cafeteria plate:** most food still goes to the food-bank truck. A waiter Optimus carries a plate across the lawn, rides the tower lift up with Elon, and he takes a bite on the way. This uses a lift trip the plan already had.
- **Transport:**
  - Small parts go in clear pneumatic tubes, and medium parts in hanging baskets and spiral slides.
  - Finished Optimus ride a big spiral slide down to crating.
  - One big open-cage lift with a bobbing counterweight carries only heavy items: cars down, coils, ingots and the Semi kit up.
  - I wrote a new lift timetable (busy about 22 of every 24 s) and updated the connector table.
- The changes are listed as "Round 3" in `CONTINUITY-CHECK.md`, and `overview.png` is regenerated.

**Part B — files**
- **Modules:** `js/style.js` (looks only), `js/rig.js`, `js/clips.js` (motion only), `js/optimus.js`, `js/elon.js`, `js/vehicles.js`, plus helpers `js/props.js` and `js/paint.js`.
- **Sheets:** `sheets.html?sheet=…` (or `?anim=…`).
- **Tools:** `tools/render.js` renders everything, `tools/check.js` runs the checks above, `tools/strip.js` makes debug frame strips.
- **README.md** documents the API.
- **Images:** `out/optimus-sheet.png`, `elon-sheet.png`, `cybercab-sheet.png`, `vehicles-sheet.png`, `overview-sheet.png`.
- **Videos:** `out/optimus-walk-carry-place.mp4`, `elon-walk-bite.mp4`, `cybercab-drive-doors.mp4` (1280×720, 30 fps).

**Rough spots**
- **Plan items for Reid:**
  - Two one-floor car drops are still there, so strictly it's more than one lift.
  - The Model Y and Cybercab line timings haven't been re-checked against the new lift times.
- **Video lengths** are 6.7 s, 7.0 s and 7.7 s, a bit over the ~4–6 s you asked for. Each loop needs a walk or drive from off-screen to off-screen.
- **Side-view shortcuts:**
  - Elon's crossed arms use a shortened-arm cheat.
  - Turning around is a quick squash-flip rather than a real turn.
  - In the bite video, Elon walks past in front of the Optimus.
- **Climbing** still looks a little crouched.
- **The plate's food** doesn't visibly shrink after Elon's bite.
- **Hands** are simple mittens; they read fine at sheet size, less so up close.
- **Cybercab size:** 4.3 m long and 1.42 m tall are assumed, not measured. The shape is matched to your description, not to photos.
- **Other vehicles:** Model Y, Cybertruck and Semi only got a quick pass. The black Model Y has a weak outline.
